title: Context cache prefetch risk matrix & GPU headroom estimates
content:
Purpose:
A compact capacity planning worksheet to evaluate the trade-offs of aggressive context-cache prefetching during a new model onboarding window. Focus is on short-term GPU headroom and risk to admission rates across regions. This is an operational planner (working sheet) not a finalized playbook.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Average active slot memory for current models: 2.8 GB 
- Average context-cache per active slot (hot prefix + KV): 420 MB
- Typical slot density per A100-80GB: 12 active slots at 70% utilization
- Baseline qps per region (steady): us-west-2=18k qps, us-east-1=22k qps, eu-west1=8k qps, asia-east1=4k qps
- Prefetch fraction = portion of onboard traffic that preloads context-cache (0.0 - 1.0)

Quick calc formulas (text):
- Projected context-cache MB = active_slots * avg_context_cache_mb * prefetch_fraction
- Additional GPU memory required = Projected context-cache MB / 1024 (GB) distributed over slots; compare to spare headroom per GPU
- Headroom pct = (Total free GPU GB across fleet in region) / (Total used GPU GB after prefetch) * 100

Region scenario table (columns: region | pool | baseline slots | avg context MB/slot | prefetch fraction | projected extra GB | estimated headroom pct | recommended throttle window)
us-west-2 | a100-pool | 5,400 active slots | 420 MB | 0.50 | 1,134 GB | 9% | 10-15m rolling
us-east-1 | a100-pool | 6,600 active slots | 420 MB | 0.65 | 1,809 GB | 6% | 20-30m rolling
eu-west1 | a100-pool | 2,400 active slots | 420 MB | 0.40 | 403 GB | 18% | 5-10m rolling
asia-east1 | v100-pool | 1,200 active slots | 460 MB | 0.30 | 166 GB | 22% | immediate safeguard

Interpretation notes:
- us-east-1 is the riskiest: high baseline slots + aggressive prefetch produces >1.8TB additional working set, reducing headroom to ~6%. If prefetch is not rate-limited, admission throttles will start tripping under normal variance.
- asia-east1 uses older HW (v100); context caches are slightly larger in practice due to tokenization differences. Despite lower qps, single-GPU headroom is tighter per-GPU because slot density is lower.

Sensitivity mini-matrix (three scenarios, headroom change):
- Base (prefetch fraction as above): us-west-2=9%, us-east-1=6%, eu-west1=18%, asia-east1=22%
- High-context (avg context +30%): us-west-2=3%, us-east-1=1%, eu-west1=12%, asia-east1=15%
- Conservative-prefetch (reduce prefetch by 50%): us-west-2=17%, us-east-1=14%, eu-west1=28%, asia-east1=31%

Operational recommendations (short list):
- For any onboarding cohort >25k qps equivalent cluster-wide, require staged prefetch gates: 10 min -> 30 min -> open, with defensive rollback at 3% headroom threshold.
- Implement region-level prefetch budgets (GB/day) to prevent one region from absorbing fleet-wide cache budgets.
- Shadow prefetch (no-op caching) run for first 2 hours to collect real context size histogram per model variant; use observed medians to update avg_context_cache_mb.
- Add a lightweight probe that measures per-slot eviction churn every 1 minute during rollouts; alert if churn rate > 0.08 evictions/slot/min.

Action items and owners:
- Ethan: add prefetch budget controls to admission API (prototype) — due 2026-03-09
- Aisha: run 6-hour shadow prefetch experiment for new-model X (collect histograms) — due 2026-02-21
- Liam: simulate aggressive onboarding using historical ingress traces and produce a 48h headroom timeline — due 2026-03-05

Open questions / uncertainties:
- How much of the onboard traffic uses long-tail prefixes that bloat the KV beyond the 420MB estimate? (need sampling)
- Is per-GPU cohabitation (multi-tenant slots) increasing effective eviction churn beyond what aggregated metrics show?

Appendix: quick simulation notes (how numbers were derived):
- Projected extra GB = sum_over_slots(avg_context_cache_mb * prefetch_fraction) / 1024
- Headroom pct computed using current fleet inventory table (refer to linked artifacts).
- This sheet intentionally uses conservative avg context sizes; update after Aisha's histogram sample.

Summary:
This working sheet recommends adding short-term prefetch budgets and a staged rollout gate to protect headroom during model onboarding. Primary immediate work: shadow sampling and a prototype prefetch budget control in the admission API.
